content.text: Community members expressed significant frustration over the dramatic decline of the Eliza token, which fell from a peak market cap of approximately 2.4 billion dollars to around 4 million dollars. Several users described the token as effectively dead with no clear path to recovery. Questions were raised about exchange listings beyond Kraken and whether any meaningful announcements were forthcoming. One user noted an app appeared ready but questioned why it was not being promoted on official social media channels.

User paolin raised concerns that official ElizaOS channels including Discord, X, and Farcaster have been largely inactive since late May, arguing the silence is damaging community trust and potential investor interest. Paolin noted Shaw had previously pinned messages stating both Milady and Eliza v3 were nearing completion but no release date has been announced for the Eliza app. Paolin also proposed a token utility model where users would need to purchase and lock up ElizaOS tokens to access plugins and services. User J_CHOY pushed back, pointing to GitHub activity and Shaw's posts on X as evidence of active development. User Omid Sa clarified that Eliza V3 was released some time ago and can be accessed by cloning the main repository, and publicly requested that Shaw reinstate community member odlitime to the Discord.

A court document was shared indicating that the lawsuit involving plaintiff Gorka Pikabea and the appearing defendants was dismissed with prejudice following a settlement, with the court retaining jurisdiction for 30 days to enforce the agreement. The dismissal was signed by Judge Jed S. Rakoff on July 8, 2026.

Storj was mentioned as having filed for bankruptcy in general community discussion. A new member named deedee joined and noted token values had dropped significantly, making selling tokens less worthwhile. Multiple users including Ginga, so, and Bek posted seeking or offering developer roles across the week, with one post specifically seeking a U.S.-based software developer with at least five years of experience.

Emmanuel announced the GOATNetwork Builder Grants Program, seeking teams building working products or MVPs, revenue-ready applications, AI agents solving real user problems, and agent-native apps that create repeatable onchain economic activity. Project types of interest include coding agents, research tools, workflow automation, sales and support agents, and agent-to-agent applications. Emmanuel offered to connect qualifying projects with the GOAT team via direct message.

PnL Labs announced the release of plugin-pnllabs, a new plugin for Solana traders that allows agents to verify information before acting, including wallet trust based on realized on-chain profit and loss data, token safety checks, real trade cost analysis, and funding forensics. The team noted they audited 30 tracked smart money wallets and found roughly half were actually losing money. The plugin is available via npm install with a free tier requiring no API key, and uses a pay-per-call model through x402 after the free tier.

Coopa v4.0 was announced twice across the week by users Kenhinde and Selcuk. The platform is described as a zero-trust digital data sovereignty platform built on Irys for permanent and immutable data storage, using wallet-based identity with no traditional cloud storage and full client-side encryption before storing files and messages on Irys and Arweave. It has been deployed on the Sepolia testnet and is accessible at coopaassistant.com. The team is seeking power users to stress-test the architecture. Separately, user x402 Data Hub announced a real-time data API for autonomous AI agents providing LLM latency data, AI API pricing, cloud GPU rental indexes, and gas rates via HTTP 402 micro-payments at 0.01 USDC on Base and Arbitrum, with 50 free daily requests per dataset.

A suspicious recruitment message was posted by user Thehuuhs advertising job openings for the Shape3 ecosystem, claiming to seek Community Managers at 20-40 dollars per hour and Growth and Marketing Managers at 40-140 dollars per hour with remote work and upfront payment. The same message was cross-posted in both the discussion and coders channels, suggesting coordinated spam activity. In the coders channel, new members introduced themselves including a digital artist named Issa offering animation and banner skills, and a user asking how to get started contributing to eliza.army. Documentation is available at docs.elizaos.ai.
